title: Restoring Coral Reefs
instructions: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Coral reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, yet they are home to roughly a quarter of all marine species. They protect coastlines from storms, and hundreds of millions of people depend on them for food and income. They are also in serious trouble. A reef is built by colonies of tiny animals called polyps, which live in partnership with microscopic algae inside their tissues; the algae supply most of the coral's food and give it its colour. When the water becomes too warm, the coral expels the algae and turns white, a process known as bleaching. If the heat persists for more than a few weeks, the coral starves. Bleaching on a large scale was almost unknown before the 1980s. It now occurs somewhere in the tropics almost every year.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Faced with these losses, a growing number of scientists and volunteers have turned from studying reefs to trying to rebuild them. The oldest method is known as coral gardening. Small pieces are broken from healthy colonies and hung on underwater frames, which look rather like washing lines, in sheltered water. After a year or so, when they have grown large enough, divers fix them to a damaged reef with cement or cable ties. The technique is simple and can be taught to local fishermen and tourists in a few days, which has made it popular with community projects from the Caribbean to Indonesia.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Its weakness is speed. The massive, rounded corals that form the main structure of a reef may grow only a few millimetres a year. A partial answer was found by accident in Florida by the biologist David Vaughan. While moving a colony in his laboratory tank, he broke it into tiny pieces, and assumed they would die. Instead, he noticed some weeks later, the fragments had grown many times faster than the original colony – as though the coral were hurrying to repair a wound. Moreover, when fragments from the same colony were placed side by side, they fused into a single sheet. By this method, known as microfragmentation, a coral that would take decades to reach the size of a dinner plate can do so in two or three years.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Both methods share a limitation: every new coral is a copy of its parent, so a restored reef may contain very little genetic variety and could be wiped out by a single disease. A different approach works with the way corals naturally reproduce. On a few nights each year, usually after a full moon, the corals of a reef release enormous quantities of eggs and sperm at the same time. The Australian researcher Peter Harrison, who was among those who first described this event on the Great Barrier Reef in the 1980s, collects the spawn in floating enclosures, keeps the resulting larvae safe from predators for several days, and then releases them over damaged areas, where they settle and grow. Since each larva has two different parents, variety is preserved.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: None of this helps if the water simply grows too hot again. A more controversial line of research therefore aims to change the corals themselves. In Hawaii, the late Ruth Gates began breeding from individuals that had survived severe bleaching, in the hope of producing offspring better able to tolerate heat; other laboratories are experimenting with supplying corals with tougher strains of algae. Gates called the approach 'assisted evolution'. Some conservationists are uneasy about releasing deliberately altered organisms into the wild. Her answer was that the alternative, doing nothing, carried the greater risk.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The most serious objection to restoration concerns scale rather than method. Even the largest projects have replanted areas measured in hectares, and at a cost of many thousands of dollars for each one. The Great Barrier Reef alone extends over some 344,000 square kilometres. There is a further worry that well-publicised restoration schemes, which make attractive stories for tourists and sponsors, give the false impression that the problem is being solved, and so weaken the pressure to deal with its cause.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Those who do the work mostly accept these criticisms. Few of them claim that reefs can be gardened back to health while the oceans continue to warm. Their argument is more modest: that restoration can keep particular reefs alive – those most valuable to local fishing or tourism, or those that supply larvae to other reefs downstream – and can preserve a variety of corals from which recovery might one day spread. Restoration, in this view, is a way of buying time. Whether the time is used depends on decisions taken a long way from the sea.

groups.instruction:
Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A–G.
Which paragraph contains the following information?
groups.limit: Write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 14–18.

items.text: an account of a discovery that was made unintentionally
a concern that restoration work may reduce efforts to tackle the origin of the problem
an explanation of the relationship between coral and another organism
a reason why one technique has been widely adopted by non-specialists
a reference to the time of the month at which a natural event usually takes place

items.stem: According to paragraph A, bleaching occurs when coral

options.A: is attacked by the algae living inside it.
options.B: gets rid of the algae that provide its food.
options.C: grows too quickly in warm water.
options.D: is damaged by storms along the coast.

items.stem: What disadvantage of coral gardening and microfragmentation is described in paragraph D?

options.B: They can be carried out on only a few nights each year.
options.C: They produce corals with little genetic variety.
options.D: They expose young corals to predators.

items.stem: Ruth Gates responded to criticism of her work by arguing that

options.A: failing to act would be more dangerous.
options.B: her corals would never be released into the sea.
options.C: other laboratories were doing similar research.

items.stem: According to paragraph G, what do most people involved in restoration believe?

options.A: Restoration will be enough to save the world's reefs.
options.B: Critics have exaggerated the cost of their work.
options.C: Tourism does more harm to reefs than warming seas.
options.D: Restoration is worthwhile as a temporary measure for selected reefs.

groups.limit: Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

rows.text: In coral gardening, pieces of coral are hung on underwater {23} until they are large enough.
Divers attach the young corals to a damaged reef using cable ties or {24}.
When Vaughan put fragments from one colony next to each other, they {25} into a single sheet.
Harrison keeps coral larvae safe from {26} for several days before releasing them.

questions.explain:
答案是 C。C 段說這個辦法 was found by accident：Vaughan 在搬動珊瑚時不小心把它弄碎，以為碎片會死，結果反而長得快很多。
同義轉換：by accident ＝ unintentionally。
questions.quote: A partial answer was found by accident in Florida by the biologist David Vaughan.

questions.explain:
答案是 F。F 段擔心廣受宣傳的復育計畫給人問題正在解決的錯覺，and so weaken the pressure to deal with its cause。
同義轉換：weaken the pressure ＝ reduce efforts；deal with its cause ＝ tackle the origin of the problem。
陷阱：G 段的人接受了這些批評，但提出這個擔憂的是 F 段。
questions.quote: give the false impression that the problem is being solved, and so weaken the pressure to deal with its cause

questions.explain:
答案是 A。A 段說明珊瑚蟲和體內的微小藻類 live in partnership：藻類提供珊瑚大部分的食物和顏色。
陷阱：E 段也提到 algae，但只是說有實驗室嘗試給珊瑚更耐熱的藻類，沒有解釋兩者的關係。
questions.quote: which live in partnership with microscopic algae inside their tissues

questions.explain:
答案是 B。珊瑚園藝法簡單，幾天就能教會當地漁民和遊客，which has made it popular with community projects。
同義轉換：local fishermen and tourists ＝ non-specialists；popular with community projects ＝ widely adopted。
questions.quote: The technique is simple and can be taught to local fishermen and tourists in a few days

questions.explain:
答案是 D。D 段提到珊瑚 On a few nights each year, usually after a full moon 同時釋放大量的卵和精子。
解題關鍵：a natural event 指珊瑚集體產卵，the time 對應 after a full moon。
questions.quote: On a few nights each year, usually after a full moon, the corals of a reef release enormous quantities of eggs and sperm at the same time.

questions.explain:
答案是 B。水溫太高時，the coral expels the algae and turns white，而這些藻類原本 supply most of the coral's food。
同義轉換：expels ＝ gets rid of。
陷阱：A 把關係說反了，是珊瑚把藻類排出去，不是藻類攻擊珊瑚。
questions.quote: When the water becomes too warm, the coral expels the algae and turns white, a process known as bleaching.

questions.explain:
答案是 C。D 段第一句：兩種方法都有一個限制，every new coral is a copy of its parent，所以復育的珊瑚礁 may contain very little genetic variety。
陷阱：B 的「每年只有幾個晚上」是珊瑚自然產卵的時間，D 的 predators 是 Harrison 保護幼蟲時提到的，都不是前兩種方法的缺點。
questions.quote: every new coral is a copy of its parent, so a restored reef may contain very little genetic variety

questions.explain:
答案是 A。面對保育人士的不安，Her answer was that the alternative, doing nothing, carried the greater risk。
同義轉換：doing nothing ＝ failing to act；carried the greater risk ＝ would be more dangerous。
questions.quote: Her answer was that the alternative, doing nothing, carried the greater risk.

questions.explain:
答案是 D。他們的主張比較謙虛：復育能讓 particular reefs 活下去，Restoration, in this view, is a way of buying time。
陷阱：A 被直接否定（Few of them claim that reefs can be gardened back to health）；B 也不對，因為他們 mostly accept these criticisms。
questions.quote: Restoration, in this view, is a way of buying time.

questions.explain:
答案是 frames（架子）。小塊珊瑚被 hung on underwater frames，看起來有點像曬衣繩。
陷阱：washing lines 只是比喻（look rather like），而且是兩個字，不符合 ONE WORD ONLY。
questions.quote: hung on underwater frames, which look rather like washing lines, in sheltered water

questions.explain:
答案是 cement（水泥）。潛水員 fix them to a damaged reef with cement or cable ties。
解題關鍵：題目已經寫出 cable ties，另一種材料就是答案。
questions.quote: divers fix them to a damaged reef with cement or cable ties

questions.explain:
答案是 fused（融合）。同一個群體的碎片並排放置時，they fused into a single sheet。
注意：題目是過去式的敘述，要照原文填 fused。
questions.quote: when fragments from the same colony were placed side by side, they fused into a single sheet

questions.explain:
答案是 predators（掠食者）。Harrison keeps the resulting larvae safe from predators for several days。
解題關鍵：safe from 之後的名詞就是答案。
questions.quote: keeps the resulting larvae safe from predators for several days
